headline: Reference-free interface scoring and low-distortion mapping extend geometric analysis of protein-protein interfaces
label: Protein Interface Quality Assessment
summary: MDQ and TopoPPI offer new ways to score and visualize protein-protein interfaces, alongside work on coarse-grained models and ensemble generation.
synthesis: The dominant thread is quantitative geometric treatment of protein-protein interfaces. MDQ is a symmetric, reference-free, DockQ-inspired score that compares interfaces across molecular dynamics frames and yields a distance metric for clustering. TopoPPI, the one published article, extends OptCuts with a contact-weighted penalty to map interfaces into low-distortion 2D atlases for visualization. The new element is interface comparison without a reference structure, and contact-weighted geometric mapping. The remaining preprints are structurally related but do not share this focus: they cover topological chunking for simulated-annealing sequence design, coarse-graining choices in machine-learned protein models, IDP ensemble generation from sequence-derived geometric priors, and AlphaFold-supported analysis of NCF1. Their outputs and benchmarks differ, so results are not directly comparable.
